guesses.reason: Short dense coat with gray mackerel tabby striping overlaid by soft orange-peach patches on the back and a peachy hind paw marks a classic torbie (tortoiseshell-tabby) domestic shorthair.
The muted blue-gray tone with narrow vertical side stripes and barred legs fits a dilute mackerel tabby pattern.
Large ears, slender build, and gooseberry-gold eyes give a faint Mau-like look, though the stripes rather than spots make this unlikely.

breed.appearance: A slim, young adult shorthaired cat with a cool blue-gray mackerel tabby coat striped in darker charcoal, softly washed with faint apricot-peach patches along the back and shoulders, and a peach-orange back foot. Her wedge-shaped face has a tabby 'M' on the forehead, a white muzzle and chin with long white whiskers, a rosy-pink nose, and wide round yellow-green eyes with an alert expression. She has tall, upright triangular ears with pinkish insides, barred gray legs, and wears a thin dark collar.
breed.fun_fact: Torbies blend tabby stripes with tortie patches, so every one wears a one-of-a-kind coat—just like their one-of-a-kind personalities!
